frames.narration: The cache starts empty. The database holds the real data.
First request for product 42. The application checks the cache before anything else.
A miss, so it pays the full price and asks the database (slow).
The application stores the answer in the cache, with a time to live, for next time.
Second request for the same product. This time the cache has it.
The database never saw that request. Multiply by thousands and the database stays calm.
Now the price changes in the database. The cache does not know, so it still holds the old value: it is stale.
The application invalidates the entry when it writes. (A TTL would also remove it eventually, just later.)
The next read misses, loads the fresh price, and refills the cache.
